---
# YAML Front Matter — controls the document's metadata and output settings.
# Copy (and adapt) this for your own notebooks.
title: "User guide"
author:
  - "Author NumberOne"
  - "Author NumberTwo"
date: today                  # Automatically uses the date you render the document
format:
  html:
    toc: true                # Adds a Table of Contents on the side
    toc-depth: 4             # Includes headings up to level 4 (####) in the TOC
    number-sections: false   # Numbers your sections automatically if set to true
    code-fold: false         # Keeps your code visible (set to true to hide it)
    code-annotations: hover  # Reveals code annotations when hovering
    theme: cosmo             # A clean, built-in look
    embed-resources: true    # Packages everything into a single self-contained HTML file
execute:
  echo: true                 # Shows your code in the output
  error: true                # Renders the document even if a code chunk produces an error
  freeze: false              # Re-runs all cells on every render (no caching)
jupyter: python3             # Tells Quarto to use your Python 3 kernel
---

The user guide must include:

- Class overview: A brief description of the class and the economic topic it covers.
- Getting started: Instructions for any setup required (such as handling the FRED API key) and a working example showing how to instantiate the class.
- Method documentation: Explanations of each available method, the arguments they accept, and the outputs they return.
- Example code: For your most important methods, provide short, isolated code examples showing how to use them and what output to expect.
